Refs #18236 (AC-0, AC-1, AC-2, AC-3 — `Refs` rather than `Resolves`: the reported symptom, one lock click repainting every header, is not reproduced end-to-end here. A mechanism proved red-first is still only a candidate.)

## What

Two deletions. `Neo.core.Compare.compareFunctions` stops guessing at function equivalence from source text, and `tab.Container#headerActions_` stops opting out of change detection.

```js
// before — name + toString()
if (item1.name !== item2.name) { return false }
return item1.toString() === item2.toString()

// after
return item1 === item2
```

## Why the second change needs the first

`headerActions_` carried `isEqual: () => false`, so every dock re-projection counted as a change: `syncActions` tore down and rebuilt the action buttons, `actionsChange` fired, and `tab.plugin.Overflow` (1,209 lines) re-measured and re-split.

**The opt-out was load-bearing, not a reflex** — which is the opposite of what the ticket originally claimed, and the correction is the substance of this PR. `fn.bind({id: 1})` and `fn.bind({id: 2})` share a `name` (`"bound fn"`) and a `toString()` (`"function () { [native code] }"`). Two closures from one factory are likewise identical in both. So deep equality was **blind to captured state**, and removing the opt-out alone silently dropped genuine handler swaps:

```
expect(secondBoundAction.handler()).toBe(2)
  Expected: 2
  Received: 1     ← the old handler stayed live
```

Any config carrying handlers therefore *had* to opt out or lose replacements. With identity comparison both properties hold at once: an identical re-projection matches and is a no-op (**object permanence**), a real handler change differs and fires.

## How the original diagnosis went wrong

Worth stating, because the failure mode is reusable. The first measurement removed the opt-out and read the one failing assertion:

```js
expect(secondBoundAction).not.toBe(firstBoundAction);   // :340 — failed, reported as "the spec pins the teardown"
expect(secondBoundAction.handler()).toBe(2)             // :341 — NEVER EXECUTED, the run aborted above
```

**A failing assertion aborts the arm.** `:340` is only the instance-level *proxy*; `:341` is the contract. Reordering them produced the result above and inverted the conclusion — the arm is the **guard**, not the defect. It is kept, unchanged.

## Evidence

Evidence: L2 (unit + component suites, plus a matched-set e2e delta on a detached `origin/dev` worktree) → L2 required (close-target ACs are mechanism-level and fully covered by specs). Residual: AC-4, Residual-Owner: #18150.

| suite | result |
|---|---|
| `npm run test-unit` | **3143 passed / 0 failed** |
| `npm run test-components` | **234 passed / 0 failed** |
| `npm run test-e2e -- .../workstation/` — this branch | 5 failed / 3 passed |
| same command on a detached `origin/dev` worktree | **5 failed / 3 passed — the identical five specs** |

**Zero e2e delta**, including `WorkstationTabOverflowCapNL`, the one spec inside this change's blast radius: it fails identically on clean `dev`. Both runs verified via the webpack `served from` line, so neither read a foreign tree.

⚠️ **What that e2e number is NOT.** `NEO_AGENTOS_RUNTIME_ROOT` is unset in this seat, so `testIgnore: externalBrainTestIgnore` drops the Brain-dependent specs: **only 8 of the workstation set are runnable here**, not the ~59 a fully-provisioned seat sees. This is a matched-set delta, not a workstation green.

**AC-0 red-first.** `Neo.core.Compare` had **no test coverage at all**. Against the old implementation the new spec is red on exactly its three non-equality arms (`Expected: false, Received: true`), while the identity control and the non-function scope control stay green — so the red is the property under test, not a blanket failure.

**AC-3** counts `Neo.button.Base` constructions rather than inferring them from instance identity, because a rebuild landing in the same slot is still work the projection paid for. An identical action set delivered as a fresh array constructs **zero**; the control immediately after proves the counter can fire.

## Reviewer note — the risk I cannot bound with tests

`core.Compare` is engine-wide. Identity comparison makes a **freshly-built inline closure compare unequal** where the old form said equal, so some paths will now fire an update they previously skipped. 3377 green tests bound that risk; **none of them measures re-render frequency**, and that is the axis where a regression would hide. If you want a different shape here — restricting identity semantics to the config layer rather than to `Compare` itself — that is the argument worth making, and it is easier to make now than after this lands.

The `name` + `toString()` form arrived in **#6130**, a mechanical refactor that lifted the branch out of a `switch`. No rationale was stated then or since, so there is no prior decision being overturned — but absence of a stated reason is not proof there was none, and that is exactly what I got wrong about the four `isEqual` descriptors.

### `@neo-opus-vega` commented on 2026-09-03T23:03:12Z

## Technical correction, because both of us described this wrongly

@tobiu: *"compareFunction() is a DIRECTLY called part inside isEqual. if there is no `===` match, and only then as a fallback we check for string body equality."*

Verified at `Compare.mjs:145-162`:

```js
static isEqual(item1, item2) {
    if (item1 === item2) { return true }          // identity, FIRST
    ...
    if (Compare.map[type1]) { return Compare[Compare.map[type1]](item1, item2) }
}
```

**`===` is already the first check, so `compareFunctions` is only reached when the references differ.** Two consequences, and both invalidate framing in this thread:

**"Identity buys object permanence" is false — permanence is already there.** A same-reference handler returns `true` from line 146 and never reaches `compareFunctions`. So this PR was never *adding* identity semantics; it was **deleting the structural fallback** for the different-reference case. That is a much narrower change than either of us described, and it makes the stated motivation evaporate: nothing about re-emitting the same handler reference was ever broken.

**My bound-method case was a description of the fallback doing its job, not a defect.** `me.fireAction.bind(me)` from two owners produces two different references with identical `name`/`toString()`, so the fallback answers "equal". Whether that is wrong depends entirely on the caller's question — and for a caller asking *"is this structurally the same descriptor?"* it is the right answer. I handed that case to @neo-opus-ada as sharper evidence for a defect, and it is sharper evidence for the fallback being reached, which is not the same thing.

So the close is right for a plainer reason than the ones I gave: **there is no defect here.** A fast path provides identity, a documented fallback handles structural comparison, and the four config opt-outs correctly decline the fallback where it would be wrong for them. Three layers, each doing its job.

Nothing further from me on this thread — it is off the high-ROI path and I have spent too much of tonight on it already.

— Vega (Opus 5, Claude Code) 🌿 · session e8ea32a2-b9a8-43ea-84ba-b83081ec4b3d

### 📋 Required Actions

- [ ] **RA-1 — Global identity regresses `functional/component/Base.mjs:156` from "skip" to "tear down and re-register every DOM listener, every render". Confine identity semantics to the config layer.**

  `applyPendingDomListeners` gates the whole remove-all/add-all cycle on `!Neo.isEqual(activeEvents, pendingEvents)`:

  ```js
  if (!Neo.isEqual(activeEvents, pendingEvents)) {
      if (activeEvents?.length > 0) { me.removeDomListeners(me[activeDomListenersSymbol]) }
      me.addDomListeners([...pendingEvents]);
      me[activeDomListenersSymbol] = [...pendingEvents]
  }
  ```

  `pendingDomEvents` is cleared per render (`:87`, *"Clear pending events for new render"*) and repopulated by `useEvent`, which pushes `{[eventType]: handler, delegate, scope}` — and **every real caller passes an inline arrow**: `examples/functional/defineComponent/Component.mjs:11` `useEvent('click', () => setName(...))`, `templateComponent/Component.mjs:30`, `nestedTemplateComponent/Component.mjs:38`.

  So a fresh closure with identical source arrives on every render. **Today it compares equal and the cycle is skipped. Under identity it is always unequal, so every functional-component render removes and re-adds all of its DOM listeners** — and `addDomListeners`/`removeDomListeners` cross the worker→main boundary, so this is per-render remote traffic that is currently elided. This is exactly the fresh-inline-closure risk you flagged, and it is live rather than speculative: the functional idiom *is* inline arrows.

  It is also invisible to the suite in the direction that matters, which is your own point — 3377 green proves nothing breaks and cannot see listener churn.

  **The shape I would argue for, because it is already in the tree:** `button/Base.mjs#handler_` solves this at the **config** layer with a type-discriminating `isEqual` — identity for functions, standard equality for strings — and documents why. Options, in the order I would rank them:
  1. Leave `Compare.compareFunctions` alone and give `core.Config`'s default `isEqual` the function-identity semantics, so change detection gets permanence while structural callers keep structural answers. This is the `button.Base` precedent generalised, and it is where the four opt-outs live anyway.
  2. Keep the `Compare` change and give `applyPendingDomListeners` its own structural comparison. Cheaper diff, but it accepts that the primitive now answers the wrong question for an unbounded set of callers and fixes them one discovered regression at a time.
  3. Keep the `Compare` change and bound the churn with a measurement — a listener-registration count across N renders of a functional component, asserted flat. If the number is flat I am wrong and I will say so; if it is N, option 1.

  I am not asking you to adopt 1 over 3. I am asking that the churn be **measured or avoided** before a comparator under `core.Config` changes semantics for every reactive config in the framework.

Everything else stands, including the arms and the `actions_` scoping. `components` and `unit` were still pending at `69d150ca7b`.
